f: What is the Child Tax Credit (CTC)?
b: A credit of up to $2,200 (2025) for each qualifying child under 17 with an SSN; partly refundable through the Additional Child Tax Credit

f: What is the Additional Child Tax Credit (ACTC)?
b: The refundable part of the child tax credit, up to $1,700 per child for 2025, based on earned income over $2,500

f: What is the Credit for Other Dependents (ODC)?
b: A $500 nonrefundable credit for dependents who don't qualify for the child tax credit, such as children 17 or older and dependent parents

f: What is the Earned Income Credit (EIC or EITC)?
b: A refundable credit for low-to-moderate-income workers; larger with qualifying children; denied if investment income is too high

f: What is the American Opportunity Tax Credit (AOTC)?
b: An education credit up to $2,500 per student for the first 4 years of college; 40% refundable

f: What is the Lifetime Learning Credit (LLC)?
b: A nonrefundable education credit of 20% of up to $10,000 of tuition per return, for any year of study including job-skill courses

f: What is the Child and Dependent Care Credit?
b: A nonrefundable credit (2025) for a percentage of care costs for a child under 13 or a disabled dependent or spouse, so you can work

f: What is the Premium Tax Credit (PTC)?
b: A refundable credit that helps pay for Marketplace health insurance; advance payments are reconciled on Form 8962
A credit for qualified adoption expenses, up to $17,280 per child for 2025, with up to $5,000 refundable

f: What is the Foreign Tax Credit (FTC)?
b: A nonrefundable credit for income taxes paid to a foreign country, so the same income isn't taxed twice

f: What is the Credit for the Elderly or the Disabled?
b: A small nonrefundable credit for people 65 or older, or retired on permanent and total disability, with very low income

f: What is the Residential Clean Energy Credit?
b: A 30% nonrefundable credit for solar, wind, geothermal and battery storage on a home; unused credit carries forward; ends after 2025

f: What is the Energy Efficient Home Improvement Credit?
b: A 30% nonrefundable credit, capped each year, for insulation, windows, doors, heat pumps and energy audits; ends after 2025

f: What is the Clean Vehicle Credit?
b: A credit up to $7,500 for a new qualifying electric vehicle ($4,000 for a used one), for vehicles acquired by September 30, 2025

f: What is the Credit for Prior Year Minimum Tax?
b: A credit that gives back AMT paid in an earlier year on timing items such as incentive stock options
EIC, Additional Child Tax Credit, 40% of the AOTC, Premium Tax Credit, up to $5,000 of the adoption credit, and excess Social Security withheld
Credit for other dependents, Lifetime Learning Credit, child and dependent care credit, saver's credit, foreign tax credit, elderly/disabled credit, energy credits
A nonrefundable credit can only reduce tax to zero. A refundable credit is paid out even if it is more than the tax
A deduction lowers taxable income, so it saves tax at your tax rate. A credit lowers the tax itself, dollar for dollar
A fixed amount by filing status that reduces income if you don't itemize; larger for age 65+ or blind
Actual expenses listed on Schedule A (medical, taxes, mortgage interest, charity, casualty) taken instead of the standard deduction when they total more

f: What is an adjustment to income (above-the-line deduction)?

f: What is the home mortgage interest deduction?
b: An itemized deduction for interest on up to $750,000 of debt used to buy, build or improve a main or second home

f: What is the charitable contribution deduction?
b: An itemized deduction for gifts of cash or property to qualified charities, limited to a percentage of AGI

f: What is the medical expense deduction?
b: An itemized deduction for unreimbursed medical and dental costs above 7.5% of AGI

f: What is the casualty loss deduction?
b: An itemized deduction for sudden losses to personal property in a federally declared disaster, after $100 and 10% of AGI
A deduction of up to 20% of qualified business income from a sole proprietorship, partnership or S corporation; taken after AGI, with or without itemizing

f: What is the student loan interest deduction?

f: What is the educator expense deduction?

An adjustment for your own contributions to a Health Savings Account when covered by a high-deductible health plan

f: What is the self-employed health insurance deduction?

f: What is the deduction for half of self-employment tax?
